pros: Good features: Comes with an 8-inch touchscreen, a 7-inch digital driver’s display, a wireless phone charger, and a Lane-watch camera

Comes with good daily use features and does not leave you wanting for more
Gets refined engine options and a great real-world fuel efficiency with the strong hybrid setup
cons: Headroom in both the front and the rear seats is limited and tall people will struggle

The petrol engine gets loud under load due to poor cabin insulation and acceleration also takes time with the CVT

pros: Handles well: Even after being a big family SUV, it remains planted at high speeds with minimum body roll and feels stable around a corner
Light on the pocket: The strong-hybrid powertrain offers good fuel efficiency along with smooth and quick performance
Premium interiors: The cabin is covered with soft touch padding and all plastics feel smooth and sturdy
cons: Limited space: While the rear seat offers good headroom and knee room, the lack of underthigh support can cause discomfort during long journeys.
Less features: For its segment and positioning, the ZR-V offers less features than some Rs 20 lakh cars, and misses out on a few flashy pieces of equipment.

pros: Cabin experience: Fit, finish and ergonomics are on point
Great chauffeur driven car: Captain seats with electric boss mode, headrests supports, extendable under thigh support and seat ventilation
Feature rich experience: Panoramic sunroof, front and rear ventilated seats, 2 zones of climate control, and 8-speaker BOSE sound system
Offers both petrol and diesel engines with manual and automatic transmissions
cons: 3rd row is not suitable for full-sized adults
Turbo-petrol fuel efficiency is not great in the city. Expect 7-9kmpl

Feature rich experience: Panoramic sunroof, front and rear ventilated seats, 2 zones of climate control, and 8-speaker BOSE sound system
Offers both petrol and diesel engines with manual and automatic transmissions
cons: 3rd row is not suitable for full-sized adults
Turbo-petrol fuel efficiency is not great in the city. Expect 7-9kmpl

pros: Smooth and refined engine makes it new-driver friendly
Rear space: Offers a good amount of legroom and knee room with adequate underthigh support
Ride quality: Good comfort over potholes and speed breakers
Boot: 402-litres of storage space with a long and deep boot which can accommodate large bags easily
cons: Low headroom at the rear for people over 6 feet
Few feature misses like sunroof, bigger touchscreen and 360-degree camera
ISOFIX mounts limited to the top-spec variant

pros: Offers feel-good features like sunroof, 360 degree camera and 9-inch touchscreen.
Safety package: 5-star Global NCAP crash test rating and 6 airbags as standard.
Excellent boot space. Can store an entire suitcase set along with two soft bags.
High mileage: Returns around 15-16 kmpl in the city in regular driving conditions.
Looks distinctive: New design elements give it an identity different from the Swift.
Ground clearance: 163mm is more than enough to drive easily over rough roads.
Comfortable ride quality: Cushioned over regular imperfections, and limits movement on sharper potholes too.
cons: AMT transmission: Slow and jerky on the highway, and upshifts quite early leaving less usable power.
Limited headroom: Sloping roofline limits headroom for 6-footers.
Low engine refinement and performance: Feels dull with a full load and overtakes require planning.

pros: Covers the basics: Keyless entry, climate control, steering mounted controls, and cruise control.

190mm ground clearance boosts confidence in new drivers.

cons: Misses out on a few feel-good features: sunroof, leatherette upholstery, ventilated seats.
No diesel engine option — available with Venue, Nexon and Sonet.
Rear seat headroom: Sloping roofline limits space for tall passengers.

pros: Proven 5-star crash test rating with good standard safety suite.
Ride quality: Feels comfortable and plush over regular speed breakers and bad roads alike.
New cabin design features neatly integrated ambient lighting, feels youthful.
CNG boot space: Bumper integrated CNG tanks don’t eat up into the boot space!
Multiple powertrain options: mild-hybrid, strong-hybrid, CNG, manual and automatic transmission options and all-wheel drive.
Premium features: Panoramic sunroof, ventilated seats, Level-2 ADAS, 10.1-inch touchscreen and 8-speaker Infinity sound system.
Super efficient: Hybrid powertrain has a claimed efficiency of 28.65kmpl!
cons: Rivals like the Kia Seltos and MG Astor feel more premium inside.
Limited headroom: Variants with a sunroof have average rear seat headroom.
No ADAS with strong-hybrid, CNG or manual transmission variants.
Insulation: Tyre and road noise could be better controlled.

pros: Covers All The Basics: For a 7-seater priced less than some small hatchbacks, the Gravite covers all the essentials, including a good infotainment package.

Comfortable For All: Absorbs shocks with ease, settles quickly, and limits body roll to keep all passengers comfortable.

Feature misses: Equipment like auto climate control, a better quality rear view camera, and alloy wheels are sorely missed.

pros: Great highway cruiser: Sits at triple-digit speeds effortlessly with enough performance for overtakes.
Premium Features: Massaging and ventilated seats with memory function, 13-speaker Canton audio system, dual wireless phone chargers and three-zone climate control.
Rich and ergonomic cabin: Leatherette dashboard, door pads, and steering wheel feel premium, and multiple physical dials help usability.
Great practicality: Adjustable front cupholders, big door pockets with a dustbin and umbrella slots, dual gloveboxes, rear removable storage box ensure more than adequate storage spaces.
cons: Third row space: Only adequate for kids or pets.
Squeaking sounds from a few panels inside after covering 20,000 km+.

pros: Driving dynamics: Feels fun to drive without any big compromise in ride comfort
Value: Base variants offer a really good functional and convenience feature package
Boot space: Not the biggest on-paper, but very practical in real life
Elegant styling: Individual elements in connected LED lighting and illuminated Skoda wordmark at the rear looks chic
Performance: Both 1-litre and 1.5-litre turbo-petrol engines offer good performance
cons: Rear-view camera: Really poor quality and no dynamic guidelines render it almost useless in anything other than broad daylight
No ADAS features could be a miss for people who do long intercity trips
Powertrain options: No CNG, diesel or hybrid powertrain option for people looking for low-running costs

pros: 446-litre boot space is more than sufficient for 4 cabin-sized trolley bags.
Fun-to-drive: 1-litre TSI engine is fun to push hard and puts a smile on your face.
Enough features: Sunroof, ventilated and powered front seats, 10.1-inch touchscreen.
Practical. Ample space for four 6-footers. Cabin storage is very well thought out too.
cons: Fuel efficiency isn’t great, particularly in heavy city traffic. Expect 10kmpl at best.
Minor annoyances: poor camera quality, very light horn, and noisy seat ventilation blowers spoil the experience.
No diesel or CNG options available.

pros: Sleeper design: Doesn’t look overly aggressive, but is immediately recognizable to the people who know
Handles like a sports car: The steering is direct and progressive while the chassis feels like it can take on more
Performance: Smooth and easy in the city, but quick and exciting when you want to have fun
Super practical: Has enough storage spaces inside the cabin and a big boot for a long vacation
cons: Rear seats: Adequate space, but the limited sense of space makes it feel claustrophobic
Ingress egress is super inconvenient with a low roof that requires you to duck a lot.
Sound: Engine and exhaust sound a little muted for a performance-oriented car
Ride quality: Can be too stiff for our broken roads

pros: Great rear seat experience - raised under thigh support and ample legroom offers great space for two average sized adults.
Feature rich - 10.25-inch touchscreen, 10.25-inch digital driver’s display, and an electric sunroof make it a well-equipped hatchback.
Sharp looking - the redesigned grille, flush-fitting door handles, and connected tail lights give it a clean and modern look.
Only diesel engine option in the segment makes it more appealing to buyers who prioritize fuel efficiency.
No compromise safety - 6 standard airbags, 360-degree camera, and an already established 5-star safety rating makes it a safe option.
cons: Turbo-petrol engine not offered with the facelifted version.
Fit and finish - many panel gaps on the outside and some flimsy elements inside break the cabin quality’s consistency.
Petrol engine gets too noisy under load and has more vibrations than expected.
No diesel automatic option on sale and the diesel is limited to the one-below-top variant.

pros: Spacious cabin: Comfortably seats four adults with good headroom and legroom for the size.
Multiple powertrain options: Petrol, turbo-petrol and CNG with AMT make the Punch a versatile choice.
SUV-like design: Looks like a proper mini SUV now, with clear design cues borrowed from bigger Tata models.
Useful feature upgrades: New 7-inch digital instrument cluster and 360-degree camera add real value.
Turbo-petrol engine: One of the most affordable turbo-petrol cars in India, finally giving the Punch strong performance.
cons: Interior feels familiar: Design changes are minimal, and plastic quality is just about average for the segment.
Touch-based air-conditioning panel: It is overly sensitive to touch and often requires you to take your eyes off the road, which isn’t ideal while driving.
No turbo-petrol automatic: The missing automatic gearbox with the turbo engine limits its appeal for city buyers.
Locked fuel efficiency: Our test cars had the minimum fuel efficiency locked at 8 kmpl, which is misleading and not transparent for the users

variant: Tiago EV Creative Plus 24 Long Range
pros: Battery warranty: Bigger battery gets a 15 year warranty which offers peace of mind.
New-driver friendly: Height adjustable seats and super gentle throttle modulation make it easy to drive.
Impressive features: 10.25-inch infotainment, 360-degree camera, auto AC with rear AC vents and many other functional features are impressive for a budget car.
Looks and feels premium: Contemporary looks and material choices inside make it feel more expensive than it is.
Comfortable ride: Rides well over bad roads and feels stable at high speeds.
cons: Fit and finish: Panel gaps and inconsistent plastic panels take away from the premium experience.
No paddle shifters: Regenerative mode has to be changed via the buttons on the central console which doesn’t feel intuitive.
Boot space: Limited space in the boot is only enough for two cabin sized trolleys and a laptop bag.

pros: Covers all functional equipment: Electric ORVMs, cruise control, power windows, and auto AC
8-speaker sound system offers a good music experience

Range / battery percentage read-outs could’ve been calibrated for more accuracy
Silly feature omissions: alloy wheels, rear AC vents, rear-adjustable headrests
Only packs dual airbags, even in the top-spec variant
Outdated infotainment package: 7-inch touchscreen feels old to use with slow response times and wired Android Auto and Apple CarPlay connectivity
Paddle shifters for changing regen modes would be more intuitive than using the button on the dashboard

pros: Modern, imposing design: The redesigned face and brawnier stance look fresher and more aggressive without losing the Hilux's tough character.
Effortless engine: The proven 2.8-litre diesel is torquey and relaxed, now paired with a smoother, more polished automatic.
Improved ride comfort: Toyota has taken a good amount of sharpness out of the ride, most noticeably in the front row.
Serious off-road hardware: Ladder-frame chassis, low-range 4x4, rear diff lock and a full suite of traction electronics.
Big cabin upgrade: A completely redesigned, chunky dashboard and a far more comfortable, big-person-friendly driving position.
cons: Bulky in the city: Heavy low-speed steering and a 5,325 mm length make tight traffic and parking a chore.
Under-equipped for the price: Manual AC, a manual-dimming mirror, fabric seats and no ADAS on a truck costing around Rs 35-40 lakh on-road.
Compromised rear seat: An upright, non-reclining backrest, a high floor and no rear AC vents make the back bench a poor place for family.
Still firm over big hits: Sharp speed breakers and deep potholes still send a strong jolt through the cabin.

pros: Great space: It is one of the most spacious MPVs for the price, which offers good space for 7 adults
Practical cabin: Offers great storage spaces, AC vents in all three rows, and rear cupholders
Necessary equipment: Gets all the required features like auto AC and a touchscreen that you’ll need for your daily drives
Capable powertrain: Comes with a powerful and efficient diesel engine with a rear-wheel-drive setup
Reliable family car: Comes with Toyota’s reliable and future proof engineering
cons: Less powertrain options: Misses out on a petrol engine and an automatic powertrain
A little too expensive: Prices have gone up since its introduction and feel high for the feature list on offer
The ride quality feels a little jumpy when driving with low load

pros: Smooth performance: Throttle and regenerative braking calibration is super smooth
Interior quality: Smooth and textured plastic along with solid buttons and stalks feel rich to interact with
Good feature package: Dual digital screens, 10-way powered driver seat, ventilated front seats and ADAS.
Design: Sharp front styling is based on Toyota’s global lineup
cons: 360-degree camera: Quality is too grainy and not acceptable at this price
Rear seat experience: Underthigh support is poor even for average-sized adults and limited sense of space
Ride quality: Comfortable at low speeds but gets bouncy and doesn’t feel settled even at 60-70kmph
Regenerative braking: No physical button or paddle shifters means level of regen braking can only be changed when stationary
Boot space: Shallow and short boot means limited space to store big bags

variant: G Opt Aero Black Edition HYBRID

Not exciting: The performance feels just about adequate and you won’t get a very fun to drive experience

Powerful turbo-petrol engine: Offers an engaging drive experience and suspension set up gives you the best of both words - comfortable and sporty when you want it to be.
Spacious and practical: Offers plenty of room, lots of cubby holes and charging options. Dual wireless charging up front is a great feature.
cons: Missing features: Does not get keyless entry, powered and ventilated front seats
Not so efficient: Fuel efficiency of the large turbo-petrol engine in traffic and when driven with a heavy right foot can drop

pros: Feature-loaded: 8-inch digital driver’s display, 10.1-inch touchscreen, ventilated seats, electric sunroof are among the highlights
